title.narrative: IN National Ganga River Basin Project

description.narrative: The objectives of the National Ganga River Basin Project for India are to support the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA) in: (a) building capacity of its nascent operational-level institutions, so that they can manage the long-term Ganga clean-up and conservation program; and (b) implementing a diverse set of demonstrative investments for reducing point-source pollution loads in a sustainable manner, at priority locations on the Ganga. There are two components to the project, the first component being institutional development. The objectives of this component are to build functional capacity of the NGRBA's operational institutions at both the central and state levels, and to provide support to associated institutions for implementing the NGRBA program. Its sub-components include: (i) NGRBA operationalization and program management, (ii) technical assistance for Urban Local Body (ULB) service providers, and (iii) technical assistance for environmental regulators. The second component is the priority infrastructure investments. The objective of this component is to finance demonstrative infrastructure investments to reduce pollution loads in priority locations on the river. The four main sectors of investments are: municipal wastewater management, industrial pollution control, solid waste management and river front management. The investments are intended to exemplify, among other attributes, the high standards of technical preparation and implementation, sustainability of operations, and public participation envisaged in the NGRBA framework. This component will also support innovative pilots, for new and transformative technologies or implementation arrangements.

title.narrative: Share of grievances addressed within 30 days from receipt

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 125%. This indicator was added at 5th Restructuring. It complemented another intermediate indicator, 'Grievance Redressal System in place at the national level, in each State and at sites of each sub-project'. All grievances were addressed, either at the investment site level or after escalation to State/Centre level in a timely manner. </p>

title.narrative: % of targeted river front management investments completed

comment.narrative: <p>Target was 100 percent achieved. The project only supported one RFD investment at Patna. The design was more complicated than typical <em>ghat </em>rehabilitations under the Ganga Program and included the development of a promenade and pedestrian walkway that connected 16 <em>ghats. </em>???????The impact of this investment is summarized in Section II.E.</p>

title.narrative: Amount of BOD pollution load abated by sewage treatment plants built or rehabilitated under the Project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 106 percent of target. Indicator was added at 5th restructuring. Target was revised at 6th restructuring. Against original target, achievement was 83.1 percent. NMCG calculated these results using the assumption that raw sewage from sewerage networks has inflow BOD of 150 mg/l and wastewater from I&D schemes has inflow BOD of 100 mg/l. Waste water quality reports produced by independent laboratories between May and August 2022 for various STPs support these assumptions. BOD of STP outflow (treated wastewater) was assumed to be less than 20 mg/l. As per Ministry of Environment, Forests, and Climate ChangeNotification G.S.R. 1265(E) dated, October 13, 2017, STP outflow BOD in Kolkata (Metro City), West Bengal State was required to be less than 20 mg/l, while for all other cities in the project the applicable permissible level was less than 30 mg/l. An Order by the National Green Tribunal in 2019 (in application number 1069/2018) reduced the permissible level to less than 10 mg/l. STPs that were already operating were given a grace period of five years to comply with these standards. At closing, STP compliance varied depending on when the investments were completed. Only the STPs in Anupshahr city (Uttar Pradesh) were not in compliance with the relevant permissible limit for BOD due to inflow that was in excess of the treatment capacity. BOD abatement figures reported in the RF are sound and accurately represent the achievement of the Project.  </p>

title.narrative: Length of sewerage network laid under the Project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 98 percent against the revised target. The indicator was added at the 5th Restructuring with a target of 3,570 km, against which the achievement was 74 percent. The achievement at closing was higher than that reported in the last ISR as physical progress under ten investment contracts had increased between 10th December and 30th December 2021. </p>

<p>The indicator was added at 1st restructuring as a core sector indicator. As no outcomes or outputs linked to project beneficiaries were increased at 1st restructuring, the ICR assumes the target for total beneficiaries at 1st restructuring reflects the ambition of the project at appraisal. The target was increased at 5th restructuring to 4.0 million and reduced at 6th restructuring to 3.57. The final revised target was 105 percent achieved. Against the target at appraisal and 1st restructuring, it was 177 percent achieved. The indicator used the total population covered by the service area of the investments - sewerage networks, STPs, I&D schemes. Since the Project also led to an increase in households getting connected to sewerage networks (see Intermediate Indicator on house service connections), the assumption that residents in the investments' catchment areas are benefit was sound. It should be noted that the measurement of project beneficiaries does not include the beneficiaries of the Patna RFD investment, which consist of residents of Patna, tourists and pilgrims (please see ICR Section II.E Other Outcomes and Impacts).   </p>

title.narrative: Households connected to network sanitation systems under the Project

comment.narrative: <p>98% achieved. This was added as a PDO indicator at 5th Restructuring. The target was reduced at 6th Restructuring. The Project adopted this indicator after agreement between the Task Team and NMCG that NGRBP-supported sewerage contracts can include construction of house service connections. However, NMCG had been tracking this as a NGRBA internal process monitoring indicator since appraisal. This was introduced as an intermediate indicator at 1st Restructuring, but no target was set. </p>

<p>Achievement was 100 percent of the revised target and 76 percent of target at appraisal. At appraisal the target was 450 MLD. However, STP utilization capacity of 60 percent was assumed (based on low utilization rates of STPs built under GAP), which is why thePDO indicator on volume of untreated wastewater prevented from entering the Ganga was 270 MLD. The Project investments in sewerage networks and I&D ensured high capacity-utilization of Project-supported STPs and non-project STPs. This enabled the Project to overachieve the outcome, despite underachieving the underlying output. At 5th Restructuring, the target increased to 620 MLD against which the achievement was 56 percent. The agreement to carry forward two large contacts with high STP capacity designs - (a) Howrah,Bally, and Baranagar contract (165 MLD); and (b) Digha and Kankarbagh (150 MLD) - to SNGRBP contributed significantly to this reduction. </p>

title.narrative: Volume of untreated wastewater prevented from entering the Ganga due to project interventions (MLD)

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 105 percent of target. Against original target, achievement was 150 percent. The indicator measured the total sewage inflow into STPs that were treating wastewater to the required national standard. The investments included in this indicator were (i) STPs (newly constructed and rehabilitated); (ii) sewerage networks (connected to project-supported and non-project STPs), and interception and diversion (I&D) schemes (connected to project supported and non-project supported STPs). House service connections increased the quantum of sewage flowing to STPs and therefore, also contributed to the achievement of this indicator. This was the only PDO indicator at appraisal that was still part of the RF at closing. </p>

title.narrative: Sanitation Operators with O&M management plan and related staff capacity building program approved and under implementation

comment.narrative: <p>In the final ISR, the achievement was zero as no O&M plans had been shared with the Task Team. Between final ISR and project closing, two approved O&M manuals were shared with Bank Task Team and a further three were shared during ICR preparation with evidence that the plans were drafted by operators and approved by EAs during project implementation. Thus, the indicator achievement was 125 percent at Project closing. In the Results Framework, the indicator remains tagged to Objective 1 Building Institutional Capacity. However, the ICR also uses it to measure achievement of Outcome 2, specifically to assess if investments were done in a sustainable way.   </p>

title.narrative: New Programme institutions are set up & are effectively functioning

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was added at 1st restructuring on June 24, 2015. It replaced the previous PDO indicator, 'Average Ratingof NGRBA-related institutions'. The target of the revised Indicator was 6. At closing the NMCG and SPMGs of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and West Bengal were assessed to be set up and functioning effectively. Bihar SPMG was set up, but over half the sanctioned positions were vacant and performance on key program management functions including procurement, financial management, and safeguards was poor (see Annex 6). It was assessed to not be effectively functioning. The Achievement of Outcome 1 aligns with this assessment. </p>

title.narrative: Number of cities/towns following the one-city one operator model

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 100 percent against the revised target. The indicator was added at 5th Restructuring with a target of 7, against which the achievement was 71 percent. In the 5th Restructuring Paper, the indicator phrasing was different: 'Number of contract implemented under the one city one operator model'. However, in the first ISR after restructuring the phrasing adopted was the same as in the RF at closing and the number of contracts under the model were never tracked by the RF. </p>

title.narrative: Number of Water quality monitoring stations generating real time data

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement of indicator was 85 percent. Achievement against original target was 150 percent. Indicator was added at 1st Restructuring with a baseline of 10. This was an error as CPCB had no water quality monitoring stations generating real time data in the Project area at appraisal. At MTR, real time water quality monitoring had been piloted at 10 sites in October 2012 with support from another World Bank operation (Hydrology Project II - P084632) and this may explain the baseline fiure at 1st Restructuring. The target was increased to 76 at 5th restructuring and reduced to 70 at 6th Restructuring. Achievement of the Project improved between last ISR (55 stations) and project closing. The activity was carried forward to SNGRBP and the remaining target of 10 has been achieved. The baseline at appraisal in SNGRBP was 44, reflecting the achievement of NGRBP by June 2020. This will need to be adjusted to avoid double counting of results between the two projects.</p>

title.narrative: Share of BOD pollution load from point source in priority locations abated under the Project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 101 percent. The indicator was added at 5th Restructuring to measure the removal of BOD through project investments from wastewater conveyed to STPs. Against the original target, the achievement was 103 percent.  </p>

title.narrative: Number of investments funded under the Project showing physical completion rates of 70% or more

comment.narrative:
<p>Achievement was 99 percent against revised indicator at 6th Restructuring. The indicator was added at 5th restructuring with a target of 100 percent, against which the achievement was 79 percent. The indicator was modified from "share of investments[...]" to "number of investments[...]" at the 6th Restructuring, but the target remained a share/percentage. </p>
<p>????This intermediate indicator is highly context-specific. After the partial cancellation of US$ 400 at 4th Restructuring and the agreement that SNGRBP would include selected carry-forward investments from NGRBP, this indicator set a target for construction progress given that the revised financing amount was projected to be fully disbursed by the revised closing date without some investments reaching completion. The SNGRBP would continue supporting these investments till completion. At the 5th restructuring, this was an indicator under Component 2, but was transferred to Component 1 at the 6th Restructuring. Setting targets for and tracking physical progress to prepare for a smooth transition (in terms of contract management, M&E, and financial management) reflects outcomes from both Components and measures aspects of both Outcome 1 and 2.  </p>

title.narrative: Number of cities where community outreach campaigns are being implemented to promote household connections to sewer networks

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 225 percent. This indicator was added at 5th Restructuring. At closing, community outreach campaigns were being undertaken in the cities of Praygraj, Kanpur, Narora, Anupshahar, Sahibganj, Rajmahal, Halisahar, Budge-Budge and Barrackpore. All cities, except Budge-Budge, witnessed an uptake in house connections to sewerage networks. It is difficult to attribute this outcome to the community outreach campaigns as investment contracts under the project were modified to include house connections. However, as an output of the multi-faceted communications program of the Ganga program, this activity was substantially overachieved. </p>

title.narrative: Infrastructure investments by value with 10 years or more of O&M including DBOT or PPP Hybrid Annuity under the Project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 100 percent against revised target. The indicator was added at 5th Restructuring with a target of 100 percent, against which the achievement is 95 percent. The ISRs that followed after the restructuring tracked the indicator against an endtarget of 90 percent. The target of 100 percent was never used in the RF. It was also unlikely to be achieved since the Project was already supporting the Patna RFD investment, which was about 5% of total investment value under Component 2, and did not have any contractual O&M arrangements. The indicator is used to assess both Outcome 1 and 2.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of planned professional staff positions filled in NMCG central and state-level institutions

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 75 percent. 128 positions were filled against a target of 161 'sanctioned' positions across the six Program institutions. Sanctioned positions were designated roles within the NMCG/SPMGs as per the NGRBA Program Framework, with pre-approved terms of reference and qualification criteria. This is in contrast with consultancy or temporary positions that were task or output-based. Inadequate availability of qualified staff, inflexibility in hiring criteria, and low staff retention affected the achievement of this intermediate outcome. However, the impact of this on project management and Outcome 1 was mitigated by engaging a PMC and hiring individual consultants. The baseline at appraisal was 5 percent. However, this consisted of MoEF staff given additional responsibilities to prepare the Project. This continued after appraisal as an interim arrangement. Effectively, the baseline was zero at appraisal since no personnel had been hired against 'sanctioned' posts as per the NGRBA Program Framework and the NMCG was not formally established till August 2011. </p>

title.narrative: Capacity building plan for regulators approved and under implementation

comment.narrative: <p>Target achievement was 100 percent. Indicator was added at 5th Restructuring. The Restructuring Paper (RP) set a target of 3 butbut this framing was never adopted by the Bank or the NMCG, who tracked progress against a "Yes/No" formulation. There was no progress reported on this in the last ISR. However, the long-running capacity building activity for CPCB, "Strengthening Environmental Regulators (SER)" was approved in 2013 and had been under implementation since then (See Section II.B). Therefore, the ICR assesses this indicator to have been fully achieved. </p>

title.narrative: Grievance Redressal System in place at the national level, in each State and at sites of each sub-project

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was 100 percent. At closing, the NMCG and all SPMGs had GRMs in place. Each State GRM was connected to investment sites and grievances that were not resolved on-site were escalated to SPMGs. Both resolved and escalated grievances were being reported. </p>

title.narrative: Number of ULBs with an approved plan for covering the O&M costs of the sanitation service beyond the project period

comment.narrative: <p>Achievement was zero percent. This indicator was added at 5th Restructuring. It replaced a similar indicator, 'ULB O&M management plans approved and implemented", which was added at 1st Restructuring with a target of 6. None of the ULB capacity building activities under Sub-component 1.B were implemented. Other interventions of the project, such as long-term DBOT or HAM-PPP contracts help reduce the impact of under-achievement on project outcomes during the life of the project. Beyond the life of the project, the SNGRBP has ULB capacity building activities and indicators in the RF to measure progress. The ICR also makes recommendations to improve ULB outcomes in Section V. </p>
